translations.text: All wisdom is from the Lord; it exists and remains with him forever.
Who can ever count the sand of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of time?
Who can fathom the heights of heaven, the breadth of the earth, and the depths of wisdom?
Wisdom was established before all things; prudence and understanding existed from eternity.
The roots of wisdom were revealed in him.
Wisdom is one, exceedingly fearsome, and sits upon the thrones of its praise.
The Lord himself established it
and spread it throughout his creation and among all flesh according to his gifts.
The fear of the Lord is glory and a source of pride, and a crown of rejoicing and gladness.
The fear of the Lord gladdens hearts and grants grace, joy, and long life.
Whoever fears the Lord will find good at the end and will be blessed on the day of his death.
The beginning of prudence is to fear the Lord. It was created with the faithful in the womb, and faithful mercy would rest upon their offspring.
The fullness of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and it fills them with its harvest
and fills all their houses with its delights.
The crown of prudence is the fear of the Lord, making peace flourish for him, together with health.
When he looked upon it and kissed it,
he exalted the understanding and wisdom of its keepers.
The roots of wisdom are fear of the Lord, and its paths lead to long life.
Unjust anger cannot be justified, for even a drop of wrath will bring ruin upon one's own soul.
The patient person must stand firm for a time and remain amid every joy until the end,
and for a time restrain his heart and hold back his words; then many lips will proclaim the praise of his wisdom.
In the treasures of his wisdom are proverbs of prudence.
Devotion to God seems contemptible in the eyes of the unjust.
You, child, desire wisdom and keep it, and the Lord will pour understanding and wisdom upon you.
For the prudence of wisdom is the fear of the Lord,
and faith and gentleness are pleasing to him.
Do not be disobedient in fearing the Lord, and do not approach him with a divided mind.
Do not be hypocritical before others, and be careful with your lips.
My child, if you come forward to serve God, prepare yourself for every trial.
Set your heart straight and make your mind firm with patience when trials come.
Stay close to the Lord and do not be faithless, so that you may be exalted in the end.
Receive joyfully every trial that comes upon you, and be patient with thanksgiving amid the pains of suffering.
For gold is tested in fire, but a person is tested in the furnaces of humiliation.
Trust in the Lord, and he will help you. Keep your paths straight and put your hope in him.
You who fear the Lord, await his mercy, and do not turn aside, lest you fall.
You who fear the Lord, look forward to good things, mercy, and everlasting joys.
Look at the generations of old and see: who trusted in the Lord and was put to shame?
And who remained in fear of him, and he abandoned him? Or who called upon him, and he delayed?
For the Lord is compassionate and merciful; he forgives sins and saves in times of distress.
Woe to cowardly hearts and weakened hands, and to the sinner who has taken two paths!
Therefore, let them not survive.
Woe to the one who has lost patience!
What will happen to him on the day of the Lord’s coming?
Let those who fear the Lord obey his words, and let those who love him keep his commandments.
Let those who fear the Lord seek what pleases him, and let those who love him be filled with his laws.
Let those who fear the Lord prepare their hearts and humble themselves before the Lord.
And let them say, “Let us fall into the hands of God, and not into human hands.”
For as his greatness is, so is his mercy, and as his name is, so are his deeds.
Children, listen to me, your father, and do this so that you may live.
For the Lord has honored the father above the son and established the father’s rights over his children.
Whoever honors his father atones for sins and stores up treasures for himself.
He brings honor to his mother.
who honors him and will rejoice in his own children.
Honor your father,
so that his blessing may blossom upon you.
A father's blessing establishes his son's household, but a mother's curses shake it to its foundations.
My child, do not exalt yourself over your father's disgrace, for his disgrace brings you no glory.
For a man's glory rests on honoring his father, and a son's disgrace is dishonoring his mother.
My child, support your father in his old age, and do not grieve him during his lifetime.
Whoever abandons his father is a blasphemer, and whoever angers his mother is cursed by the Lord.
My child, live your life with gentleness, and you will be loved by an esteemed person.
The greater you are, the more humbly you should conduct yourself, so that you may find favor before the Lord.
Great is the Lord's power, and he will be glorified by his humble ones.
My child, do not investigate what is greater than you; instead, reflect on what you have been commanded.
Do not examine what goes beyond your needs,
and do not be led astray by conjectures, for speculative minds have led many wise people's thoughts astray.
Whoever loves evil will perish in it.
A stubborn heart will be weighed down with sorrows.
There is no cure for the sufferings of the proud, for he has planted a root of bitterness within himself.
The heart of the wise will reflect on proverbs, and an attentive ear will desire wisdom.
Water extinguishes a blazing fire, and acts of mercy atone for many sins.
And at the time of his downfall, he will find help.
My child, do not withhold the livelihood of the poor,
and do not grieve the hungry. Do not anger a person in his weakness.
Do not anger the heart of one who suffers; do not delay your gifts to someone in need.
Do not disregard a servant in distress; do not turn your face away from the poor.
Do not give anyone cause to curse you,
for when someone curses you with a bitter heart, his Maker will quickly hear his prayer.
My child, make yourself beloved by the people.
And bend your knee before a ruler, and speak before him gently and peaceably.
Rescue the oppressed from the hands of their oppressors, and do not become angry when judging.
Be like a father to orphans.
And you will become a son of the Most High.
My child, wisdom has exalted her children.
And those who love her love life, and whoever seeks her early will be filled with every good thing.
Whoever receives her inherits glory, and wherever he enters, the Lord blesses him.
And whoever listens to her judges the nations.
If you have faith, you will inherit her, and her possessions will become part of your inheritance.
Pay attention to the circumstances of the time, and fear evil.
And do not take shame upon yourself.
For there is shame that brings sin, and there is shame that brings glory and joy.
My child, do not show partiality in your own case,
so that you may not be put to shame in your downfall.
Do not withhold a word when it is time to save someone. Do not conceal your wisdom.
For speech reveals wisdom, and the instruction of wisdom is revealed in the words of the tongue.
Do not oppose the truth [?]. If you are asked about something you do not know, do not consider it shameful not to know.
And do not be ashamed to confess your sins.
My child, do not show deference to the powerful.
And fight for the truth even to death, and the Lord your God will help you.
Do not be quick to speak, fainthearted, or slack in your work.
Do not act like a lion in private in your house, or [?] among your servants.
Do not be eager to stretch out your hands to receive, but reluctant to give.
And do not rely on your possessions.
Do not follow your own will and strength, and do not be proud of your treasures. Do not be self-reliant and say, “My possessions are many.”
Do not say, “Who can do me harm?” For the Lord will exact vengeance from you.
Do not say, “I sinned by doing evil; now what has happened to me?” For the Lord is patient.
Concerning your repentance and forgiveness.
For mercy and anger are in his hand, and he pours out his wrath upon sinners.
My child, do not delay turning from your sins to the Lord.
So that you do not perish because of your sins.
Do not put your hope in unjustly acquired treasures, for they will not help you on the day of wrath.
Do not walk along every path, for this is the way of a sinner and a double-tongued person.
Let good counsel be firmly established in your mind, and let the same word remain in your mouth.
Be quick to listen and patient in answering.
If wisdom comes to you, give your neighbor an answer; otherwise, keep your hand over your mouth.
Glory and dishonor are in the power of the tongue, and a person's destruction comes through his own dishonorable tongue.
Do not delight in being a slanderer, and do not stumble with your tongue.
Reproof, shame, and dishonor follow stumbling, and even more follow a double-speaking tongue.
A bad name inherits shame and dishonor, and a sinful person inherits double-tongued speech.
Do not become proud in your own counsel.
So that you do not destroy your fruit and become dishonored like a fruitless tree.
An evil soul destroys those who possess it, and that soul will be trampled underfoot by its enemies.
A person who speaks pleasantly makes many friends, and a pleasant tongue often receives praise from many.
My child, let your friends be many, but among a thousand let only one be your adviser.
If you acquire a friend, acquire him in a time of distress, but do not trust him too quickly.
For there are friends in times of affection, but on the day of anger they are nothing.
There is also a friend who takes the place of an enemy and, in a quarrel, reveals his hostility to disgrace you.
A friend who shares your table does not help you in distress.
And he will share in your good things just as you do.
But if distress comes upon you, he will become your accuser and secretly turn away from your presence.
Keep away from your enemies, and beware of a friend who serves you falsely and of someone who speaks with a double tongue.
A faithful friend is a strong tower, and whoever finds him finds a treasure.
A faithful friend has no price.
And whoever fears the Lord will be blessed with a good friend, for as he is, so also is his friend.
My child, choose wisdom in your youth, and you will find understanding until old age.
And understanding is difficult for the ignorant, because they cannot grasp it.
Prudence is true to its name, and it is not known to many.
Listen to me, my child, and accept my instruction, and do not turn away from my understanding.
Put your feet into her fetters and your neck into her collar.
Approach her with your whole mind, and keep her ways with all your strength.
Seek and investigate, and make it known to yourself.
And in the end you will find her rest.
The bonds of wisdom will be a strong protection for you, and her collars will become an ornament of gold.
And she will place a crown of joy on your head.
My child, if you wish to become discerning,
stand among the elders, and draw near to whoever is wise. Every day desire to hear the words of God, and do not let the proverbs of wisdom pass you by.
If you find someone with understanding, go to him early and often.
Meditate on the Lord's commands, and he will strengthen your heart and give you a desire for wisdom.
My child, do not do evil, and evil will not come upon you.
Keep away from the unjust, and they will be driven away from you.
Do not sow in the furrows of injustice, lest you reap sevenfold evil from it.
Do not ask the Lord for authority if you will not walk according to his will. Do not ask a king for a throne of glory if you will not be subject and obedient to his will.
Do not make a show of your words before kings.
Do not wish to become a judge if you cannot wrest justice from injustice. Do not shrink back before a ruler, lest you place a stumbling block in the way of justice.
Do not sin among the crowds in the cities, and do not give yourself over to a mob.
Do not be fainthearted in your prayers, and do not delay in showing mercy. Do not delay in carrying out God's commandments.
And do not laugh at a person whose heart is bitter, for the one who humbles also raises up.
My child, do not sow lies among brothers and friends.
Do not show off among elders, and do not repeat your words in your prayer.
Do not count yourself among the righteous, and do not consider yourself unrepentant among sinners.
Eternal fire and the undying worm are the executioner of the ungodly and sinners.
My child, do not exchange friends for a bribe, or a true brother for the gold of Ophir.
Do not forsake a friend or an understanding wife, for her favor is better than gold.
Do not anger a faithful servant who works for you, and do not scorn a hired worker who has devoted himself to your service.
Love a diligent servant, and do not deprive him of freedom.
If your beast of burden is useful, care for it and feed it.
If you have children, instruct them and bow their necks.
If you have daughters, be watchful, and do not pamper them or embolden them.
Give them to a wise man, and you will find that you have accomplished a great deed.
If your wife is to your liking, do not send her away from you; but do not entrust yourself to her if she hates you.
My child, honor your father with all your strength, and do not forget your mother’s labor pains.
Repay them as they have given to you, for through them you were born.
Fear the Lord with all your heart, and honor his priests.
Love your Creator, and do not despise his servants.
Honor the priests and give them their portion: the lobe of the liver and the kidneys with their fat.
Do good to the poor, so that your blessing may be complete.
Do not withhold your tears for the dead.
And keep your own end in mind.
Do not oppose a powerful man, lest you fall into his hands.
Do not oppose a rich man.
For gold and wealth have twisted the minds of kings.
Do not quarrel with a talkative man, for you will be piling wood on a fire.
Do not joke with a foolish man, lest he insult your ancestors.
Do not reproach someone who has turned away from sins, for we too are subject to sins.
Do not dishonor a person in old age, for you too will grow old.
My child, do not open your mouth against an abusive man, for he will rush upon you like someone lying in ambush.
Do not lend to a powerful man; if you do lend, consider it lost.
Do not stand surety for a rich man; otherwise, expect to pay the penalty.
Do not stand as an opponent against a judge, lest they judge you according to his standing.
Do not travel with a reckless man, lest he lay every burden on you; for whatever he does, he does according to his own wishes, and you will perish through his foolishness.
Do not go alone with an angry man, and do not quarrel with him, for bloodshed seems a trivial matter in his eyes.
My child, do not take counsel with a fool, for he cannot keep your words to himself.
Do not do anything secret in front of strangers, for you do not know what may befall you through them.
Do not open your heart to everyone, lest they thank you without reason.
My son, do not entrust yourself to a woman, lest she gain mastery over your strength.
Do not leer at a prostitute's face, lest you fall into her snares.
Do not hasten to singing women, lest you become entangled in troubles.
Do not gaze at a virgin, lest her beauty make you stumble.
Do not surrender yourself to prostitution, lest you lose your inheritance.
Do not roam the streets of cities, and do not stray along their paths.
My son, do not become at all familiar with a married woman, and do not gather with her to drink wine,
lest your heart turn aside and you yourself be brought to ruin.
Do not abandon an old friend, lest the new one prove unequal to him.
A new friend is new wine: if it grows old, you will drink it with joy.
Do not envy the glory of a sinful man, for you do not know his end.
Do not join in the pleasures of the ungodly, for you will not be justified.
Keep far away from anyone who has the power to kill, and if you approach him, do not offend him.
Take the measure of your strength, and weigh your words according to your ability. Make discerning people your companions, and take counsel with them.
Let righteous people be your table companions, and let those who fear the Lord be your pride.
Works will be praised for the skill of the hands, and one who is wise in speech leads the people and is held in awe among his companions.
A wise judge is an instruction to the people.
The tax collectors, too, act according to his command.
An undisciplined king destroys his forces; a city will be built up through the wisdom of its rulers.
Authority over the earth is in God's hands, and he will raise up the right person at the right time.
A man's prosperity is in the Lord's hands, and he will inscribe his glory on faces.
Do not hold a grudge against your neighbor for any offense. My child, keep away from falsehood and sins.
Pride is hateful to God and to human beings.
Kingship passes from nation to nation, and they perish because of injustice and pride.
He is a king today, and tomorrow he dies.
The beginning of pride is to depart from the Lord, for his heart has turned away from his Creator.
The Lord will overthrow the thrones of the proud.
The Lord uprooted the nations and planted the gentle and the godly in their place.
Pride was not created with humankind; therefore the Lord intensified his wrath and destroyed it.
What offspring of humankind is honorable? The offspring of those who fear the Lord is honorable. Dishonorable is the offspring who transgresses the commandment of his parents.
Among brothers, the eldest is honored, but the one who fears the Lord is more honored than he.
For the honored, the rich, and the poor, the fear of the Lord is their boast.
It is not right to dishonor a poor and wise man.
The mighty man and the ruler will be honored.
My son, honor yourself with humility.
For who will justify someone who sins against himself? Who will honor someone who dishonors his own life?
The rich man is honored for his wealth, and the poor man for his understanding.
Insight into wisdom raises the heads of the humble and seats them among rulers.
Do not marvel at a person's beauty, and do not reject a man because of his appearance.
Among flying creatures the bee is small, and its produce is fine.
Do not boast about beautiful clothes, and do not become proud on a day of glory.
Many rulers fell to the ground, and a crown was fastened upon someone whom no one expected.
Ask first, and do not slander; understand, and then speak.
Do not speak about things you do not know, and do not interrupt while others are speaking.
My son, do not involve yourself in many undertakings, for if you take on too much, you will not be able to manage it; if you pursue it, you will not catch up, and if you flee, you will not escape.
For there is someone who strives and labors, yet is found to be even more needy.
And there is someone whose strength has diminished, who is full of poverty, weak, and in need of a helper.
And suddenly the Lord looked upon him with kindness, raised him from his weakness, and lifted up his head.
Life and death, good and evil, wealth and poverty are equal before God.
Love and wisdom and the path of good deeds come from him.
Error and darkness were established because of sins. Wickedness grows old with those who walk in wickedness.
The Lord's gifts rest firmly upon the righteous.
There is wealth that comes from perseverance, and that is his portion.
When he says, “I will eat and drink from my own good things.”
And he does not know what will happen to him: he will leave it to strangers, and he himself will die.
My child, do not marvel at the deeds of the ungodly, for through [?] he acquires what is perishable. Rather, trust in the Lord.
For it is easy in the Lord’s eyes to make a poor person great.
In days of adversity, do not forget prosperity, and in days of prosperity, do not forget adversity.
Afflictions will make luxury and beauty forgotten, and a person’s end reveals his deeds.
Do not call anyone blessed before his death, for from a man’s son you will be able to take his measure.
Do not bring every person into your house, for Satan’s ambushes prepare treachery within him.
Always love a wise and self-controlled man, for the proud-hearted and deceitful man knows treachery like a spy, and his wickedness takes many forms.
Just as a dog snatches things wherever it enters, so a lawless person destroys and causes turmoil wherever he goes.
A fire flares up from a little trouble; likewise, the lawless man sheds blood like water over a small matter.
Beware of an evildoer, lest he bring you into disgrace.
My child, be discerning when doing good to someone, so that you may receive gratitude for your kindness from him.
Do good to good people, so that you may be repaid; and if not by them, then by the Most High.
Do good to the humble, and do not lend a hand to the ungodly,
so that you do not receive twice as much evil from him in return for your kindness. Indeed, the Most High also hates sinners and repays the ungodly with retribution.
In prosperity a friend is not revealed, and in adversity an enemy does not remain hidden.
Never trust your enemy, for like copper he stains the hands of those who hold him with rust.
Be careful; guard yourself against him, and be to yourself like a polished mirror.
Do not seat him at your right hand, lest he seek your place, and afterward you remember my words.
For who pities a snake charmer bitten by a snake, or someone who thrusts his hand into the mouths of wild beasts? Likewise, someone who approaches a lawless man becomes stained with his sins.
And even if he withdraws from the deed for a moment, the accomplice does not hold out.
Likewise, an enemy is sweet with his lips, but in his heart he plans to destroy you.
He squeezes out tears before you, but if he finds an opportunity, he cannot get enough of your blood.
If misfortune befalls you, you will find him there before you, hostile. He makes a show of helping you,
and shakes his head, saying, “When will I find an opportunity to destroy my friends?”
And he turns his face away, sighing, but not to see you alive again.
For whoever comes near pitch is smeared with it, and whoever trusts such a person is corrupted.
My son, do not take on a burden heavier than you can bear, and do not quarrel with someone rich and powerful.
What does an earthen pot have in common with a cauldron? For when they strike each other, the clay is shattered by the cauldron.
The rich man oppresses the poor man and then roars at him; the poor man is oppressed by the rich man and trembles before him.
Be careful not to go astray, and do not perish in your merriment.
When you are in the midst of merriment, beware of evil, for evil quickly mingles with good.
If you encounter evil people and they invite you to a feast, keep away from them, and do not let them get hold of you.
Do not plunge in yourself, lest you be ruined.
And do not trust their shifting words, for with many words he tests and examines you and laughs at you.
My son, whoever does not heed a friend's words is foolish.
For an animal loves its own kind, and a person loves his equal.
Each kind goes to its own kind, and a person to one like himself.
What likeness is there between a wolf and a lamb? Likewise, there is none between a sinner and a righteous person.
What does a hyena have in common with a dog? Likewise, there is no peace between the poor and the rich.
The wild donkey is the lion's prey in the wilderness; likewise, the destitute are food for the rich.
The arrogant person recoils from the humble, and likewise the rich person from the poor.
If the rich man falters, he is steadied by his friends, but the poor man falls because of his own friends.
If the rich man does wrong, he has many helpers, and if he speaks improperly, they justify him.
And when the poor man does wrong, they rise up against him and beat him in punishment; and if he speaks a wise word, they laugh and do not let him speak.
The rich man spoke, and everyone fell silent, and they exalted his words to the clouds.
But know this: there is recompense for both these and those, and there is a Lord.
Wealth is good where there are no sins, and poverty is evil in the mouths of the ungodly.
Whether evil or good.
A person's face reveals cheerfulness and anger.
Whoever does not stumble with his mouth,
blessed is he, and the one who has not deprived himself of hope in his Lord.
Wealth does not suit a narrow-minded man, and what use is wealth to an envious man?
Whoever is bad to himself will not be good to others.
Who is worse than someone who begrudges himself?
And in the end his wickedness will be revealed.
The eye of a greedy person is not satisfied with a portion.
For an eye inflamed with malice at the table wastes away its owner.
My child, while you are able, treat yourself well.
Remember that death will not delay.
Treat your friends well, and help him as much as you can before you die.
Do not deprive yourself of good days, and do not let a share of wisdom pass you by.
Practice righteousness before death.
And in receiving and giving, keep yourself blameless and holy.
All flesh wears out like rags, and there is no rest in hell, for the covenant of death has existed from the beginning.
Just as among the leaves on leafy trees some fall and others sprout, so among people some are born and others die.
Every work passes away, and the one who does it will depart with it.
Blessed is the man who reflects with wisdom and speaks with thoughtful understanding.
My son, from the beginning God created man with a will of his own.
He placed fire and water before him, so that he might plunge his hands into whichever he wished.
For death and life are before man.
The Lord is mighty in power; he sees everything, but he himself is not seen.
He commanded no one to act wickedly and did not desire lawlessness among people, for he also established his holy name among the holy ones.
For one righteous person who does the will of God is better than ten thousand lawless people.
My son, do not desire a multitude of worthless children if the fear of God is not among them.
Do not entrust your life to them, nor your soul’s portion, but place it in safekeeping.
And consider it better to be childless than to have ungodly children.
Fire will blaze in the assemblies of sinners, and wrath will burn against a lawless nation.
A man will be judged by his deeds.
For the sinner will not escape through his plunder, and the righteous person will not perish in his endurance.
He spared Lot during his sojourns.
And he destroyed the six hundred thousand.
For righteousness and mercy come from him. He can forgive
and repay with many rebukes.

Every merciful person will find mercy, for the righteous rewarder will judge according to deeds. The Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart so that his works might be seen beneath heaven. My child, his mercy is evident to all creatures, for he distributed light and darkness among human beings.
Do not say, “I will hide from the Lord, and who will remember me from on high?”
Or what am I among so many creatures?
Know this: heaven and the heaven of heavens, and the earth with the foundation of all the depths

all tremble and shake when he looks upon them, for his works are many. His will alone, which is hidden, [?] with great wonders, so that even fitting praise is blessed by him; for our humble praise neither diminishes him nor makes him greater.
My child, listen to me and accept my instruction,
for I will reveal
the Lord’s works from the beginning of his creation.
The Lord created humanity from the earth.
He gave them a fixed number of days and a measured span of time.
He clothed them according to their ability and their strength.
He placed dread and fear of them upon all flesh, so that they might rule over all the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven.
He equipped them with complete senses and reason.
He made good and evil known to them
and showed them the greatness of his works,
so that they might recount his glory and bless his holy name.
He added to them an understanding of crafts
and established an everlasting covenant with them.
Their eyes saw the wonders of his glory, and their ears heard his awe-inspiring words.

And he commanded them to beware of every evil and to keep the cherished commandment. The Evil One taught them wickedness and made them despise both God and the Creator’s love. He removed the sevenfold gifts from them and filled them with seven transgressions. From the earth from which they had been taken, they inherited that same cursed earth. After this he taught them sins of every kind, until their memory was wiped out by water. And through Canaan’s son they again turned to evil, speaking one common language, up to the tower that soon fell.
And the Lord divided the languages and the nations
and appointed leaders for each nation.
And after many years had passed, he took Israel as his own portion.
And his eye watched their ways.
And their lawless deeds were not hidden from him, for the sins of every person are written before him.
And a person's righteousness and grace are sealed before him.
Yet he granted sinners a return to repentance.
And suddenly, like the pupil of an eye,
he will awake and repay what is due. My child, a foolish man, led astray in his mind, speaks error.
Turn back to the Most High and abandon your sins.
Turn away from injustice and hate impurity.
Who in the underworld will praise the Most High in place of the living?
Who will offer him praise?
Praise has perished from one who has died in sins, as from one who never existed.
The living and those in good health will praise the Lord at all times.
For it is not possible for every goodness to be in a human being, since a son of man is not immortal,
but dust and ashes.
What is brighter than the sun? Yet even it grows dim.
He who lives forever created everything. The Lord alone is beyond description and righteous.
For who can examine his greatness?
And who can recount his power and his mercy?
For when a person prepares to recount his marvelous deeds, only then will he begin to recount his wonders.

The number of a person's days is perhaps a hundred years. But like a drop from the sea and a grain of sand, so are a hundred years among the sum of the ages. For a thousand years in this world are not even like one day in the world of the righteous.
For the Lord bestowed his mercy upon them because they loved him and his command.
Therefore he increased his forgiveness.
For a person's compassion is toward his neighbor, but God's compassion is toward all flesh.
He rebukes, disciplines, teaches, and brings them back, like a shepherd bringing back his flock.
He has mercy on those who heed and hasten to his ordinances, for the judgments are his.
My child, do not accompany good deeds with reproaches, or any of your gifts with sorrowful words.
Scorching heat refreshes the dew; in this way a good word brings more joy than gifts.
A foolish man insults without measure.
Learn first, and then speak. Before you engage in battle with enemies, seek a helper for yourself.
Before you fall ill, heed physicians. Before entering judgment, examine yourself.
And keep yourself humble. When you transgress, turn to repentance.
Do not wait until the hour of death to become righteous. And do not delay the vow you have made; prepare to fulfill it.
And do not put the Lord to the test.
Remember wrath on the day of the end, and the time of repayment when he turns his face away.
In a time of abundance, remember hunger, and in a day of greatness, remember poverty.
For times change from morning to evening, and everything moves swiftly before the Lord.
A wise man is obedient in everything and is on his guard at a time of sin.
Every wise person has come to know understanding
and has poured forth sound proverbs from his mind.
My son, do not indulge yourself in the pleasure of desire, and you will be trampled by your enemies.
Do not delight in luxury, and do not bind yourself to it.
And do not impoverish yourself through contributions and borrowing.
For a drunken laborer will not attain greatness. Whoever despises small things will fall little by little.
Women and wine destroy wisdom; the reckless person will perish.
Whoever is quick to believe is shallow-hearted, and whoever transgresses sins against himself.
One who is shameless in mind will be [?] to many.
Do not be eager to repeat a report to either a friend or an enemy.
If there is no sin involved, do not reveal it at all.
For he heard it and became wary of you.
Have you heard something? Let it die in your heart. Stand firm: it will not tear you open and come out.
Like an arrow lodged in a person's body, so is a report in the heart of a fool.
Reprove your friend; perhaps he has not actually transgressed. But if he has sinned, warn him again, so that your friendship may be strengthened.
There are many slanders, and you must not believe every report.
There is someone who stumbles, but not deliberately, for who has not erred in thought or in speech?
All wisdom is the fear of the Lord.
Instruction in evil is not wisdom, nor is there wisdom in the deliberations of sinners.
A person of little understanding who is God-fearing is better than one full of understanding who dares to transgress the laws.
There is genuine shrewdness that is full of wickedness and injustice.
There is someone who forfeits favors in order to make justice evident. And there is a cunning person who walks humbly in secret, whose belly is full of deceit.
A person is revealed by the very look of his eyes, and wisdom is recognized on encountering his face.
A person's clothing, the laughter on his face, and the steps of his feet tell about him.
There is a rebuke that is not good, and there is silence that is wisdom.
For it is much better to rebuke than to become angry.
And someone who administers justice by force is like this:
like a eunuch who desires a maiden's virginity.
There is someone who becomes hated by everyone because of his excessive talking.
And there are some who have no words in their mouths. There are some who are silent because they know the time for speaking.
A wise man will remain silent until the right time, but someone who is foolish and impious will rush ahead.
Someone who multiplies his words will be despised, and someone who is hated becomes excessively harsh.
There is success that brings evils upon a person, and there are gains that lead to loss.
There are gifts that offer no help, and there are gifts that bring a double return.
There is loss for the sake of glory, and there are losses for the sake of humility. There are some who lift their heads high.
And there are those who buy something great for little, and there are those who suffer a loss seven times greater.
Someone who is wise in speech makes himself beloved. The favors of fools will be put to shame.
The gifts of fools will bring no benefit, for in exchange for one thing their eyes look for many.
He gives a little and heaps on great reproaches, and opens his mouth like a herald.
The fool says this: "I have no friend, and I receive no favor from good people."
It is better to stumble with the feet than with the tongue; thus the downfall of the wicked will come swiftly.
A graceless man is an ill-timed tale.
Proverbs are dishonored in the mouth of a foolish man, because he does not speak them at the right time.
There is someone who is kept from sin by weakness and does not repent when he is at ease.
There is someone who destroys himself out of shame and perishes because of his partiality.
There is someone who takes shame upon himself for a friend and, without cause, gains him as his enemy.
A lie is an ugly stain on a person.
Theft is one thing and lying another, and both will inherit destruction.

The words of a person's own heart bring dishonor upon him, and his shame will come upon him. My child, keep my words and attend to them day and night. For even a true son and an heir of noble birth who does not renew and advance the greatness of his ancestors is a great shame and reproach to his forefathers, and a new curse.
Proverbial Sayings, Second.
Whoever is wise in speech will guide him, and a wise man will be pleasing to the great.
Offerings and bribes blind the hearts of the wise and turn them back like a wolf struck in the mouth.
Hidden wisdom and unseen treasure—what use is either of them?
Better is the person who conceals his foolishness than the one who conceals his wisdom.
My child, flee from sins as from the presence of a snake, for if you approach, it will strike you.
All lawlessness is like a double-edged sword,
and there is no healing for its wounds.
Insults and punishments will destroy greatness; likewise, the houses of the arrogant will be overthrown.
The prayers of the poor are close to God, and their pleas for justice rise swiftly.
Whoever hates correction is found on the paths of sinners, for whoever fears the Lord turns back promptly with his whole heart.
The powerful man is recognized from afar by his speech, but the wise man knows when he stumbles.
Whoever builds his house with other people's wealth is like someone who makes a heap of stones.
For a gathering of the lawless is a heap of tow, and their end is a blazing fire.
The paths of sinners are smooth and level, cleared of stones, but their end is destruction in hell.
But whoever keeps the laws gains understanding of his own thoughts,
and the outcome of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.
A person who lacks discernment does not accept instruction.
For there is cleverness that increases bitterness,
and the knowledge of the wise will overflow like a torrent and like the gushing of a spring.
The heart of a fool is like a shattered vessel, for it does not receive knowledge at all.
When the wise man hears the words of someone with understanding, he praises him and rests in him. When the uncouth man hears them, he is displeased, turns his face away, and casts them behind him.
The speech of a foolish man is a load thrown onto the road,
and wisdom is like shackles on the feet of fools.
The fool lifts himself up when he laughs, but the insightful man barely smiles with his lips.
Instruction is like a golden ornament to a wise man, and like a bracelet on his right hand.
It is foolish for a man to stand at the door and listen to what is happening inside. A wise man considers this shameful and dishonorable.
A foolish man's heart is in his mouth, but a wise man's words are weighed in his mouth and in his heart.
The ungodly person curses Satan and does not realize that he is cursing himself.
A slanderer defiles himself and is hated where he lives.
The lazy man is likened to a smeared stone, and everyone tramples on his foolishness.
The lazy man is smeared with mud, and whoever takes hold of him shakes off his hands.
Undisciplined children are a father's shame, and a daughter is a child born to poverty.
And a shameless woman brings shame on her father and mother.
Songs of sorrow are like untimely sayings. Wisdom and instruction are for the wise at all times.
One who teaches a fool is like someone patching a broken piece of pottery.
One who explains something to someone who does not listen is like someone waking a sleeper from deep sleep.
When someone explains wisdom to a foolish man and asks him for an answer, he says, 'Who are you?' or 'What did you say?'
Weep over the dead, for he has been deprived of light, and weep over the fool, for he has been deprived of wisdom.
Weep only a little over the dead, for he has found rest.
But the fool's life is worse than death.
Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but mourning for the ungodly and foolish man lasts all the days of his life.
Do not speak at length with a foolish and senseless man; do not travel with a fool.
Turn away from him, and you will find rest. Otherwise you will be implicated in his death, or he in your bloodshed.
What is heavier than lead? What is its name but 'fool'?
Sand, salt, and iron bars are easier to carry than a foolish man.
And just as a building held together by braces will not collapse during an earthquake,
so a heart firmly grounded in wise counsel will not tremble in a time of turmoil.
One who pokes an eye with a stick makes tears flow; likewise, one who provokes a person's temper reveals his own heart.
And one who insults a friend destroys the friendship.
If you draw a sword against a friend, do not give up your hope in him, for there is a way back.
Do not reproach him, and do not be afraid, for there is room for reconciliation. But do not reveal his secrets, for that is what destroys friendship.
Be faithful to your companion in his poverty, so that you may rejoice in his prosperity.
Smoke and flame come before sparks; likewise, quarrels and conflict come before bloodshed.
Who will give me a guard for my mouth and a trustworthy seal upon my lips, so that I do not fall because of it?
Lord, Father of my life and my God, do not abandon me to their plans.
And who will set stern discipline over my thoughts and wise understanding over my heart,
so that my acts of ignorance do not increase, my sins do not multiply against me, and I am not found fallen beneath the feet of my enemies?
Lord, Father and God of my life, do not give me wandering eyes,
and remove the desire of my eyes and heart from me.
Do not let bodily needs and lustful desire overcome me, and do not furnish me with the words of a shameless soul.
Listen to the instruction of wisdom, and whoever keeps it will not fall through his lips.
The proud, the blasphemer, and the lawless will fall.
Do not accustom your mouth to swearing oaths, for great ruin comes from it.
And do not make a habit of swearing by the name of the Holy One,
for whoever frequently swears oaths is not free from sins.
For if he lies, his sin rests upon him, and if he breaks his oath, the harm is doubled.
And even if he swore needlessly, he will not be justified.
For there are words of an oath that are equivalent to death. May these not be found in the inheritance of the righteous.
And do not walk in the sins of the lawless,
and do not accustom your mouth to swearing oaths with them,
so that you do not afterward open your eyes and curse the day of your birth.
There are two things that lead to repeated sin, and a third brings down wrath.
A passionate soul is like a fire: it burns and is not extinguished until it devours something.
And a man who commits sexual immorality with the members of his body does not stop until a fire blazes up.
For his flesh is sweet, and he does not stop doing evil until he dies.
For he said during his lifetime,
“Whom do I fear?
And where will the Most High remember my sins?”
He did not know that the eyes of the Lord see hidden things, and that he had determined his end.
Such a person will be convicted in the midst of the cities,
and they will seize him where he does not expect it.
Likewise, a woman who leaves her husband and obtains an heir by another man:
first, she dishonored the law of the Most High; second, she sinned against her husband; third, she committed sexual immorality through adultery.
They will bring such a woman before the court and condemn her together with her children,
so that her children’s roots may not become established and their branches may not bear fruit,
so that their memory may become a curse and may not be erased,
so that those who remain may know that nothing is better than the fear of the Lord, and nothing is sweeter than attending to the commandments of God.
Praise of Wisdom
Wisdom will praise herself;
she will open her mouth in the assemblies and boast before his hosts.
“I came from the mouth of the Most High
and covered the earth like a mist.
I dwelt in the heights, and my throne was like a pillar of cloud.
I traveled around the ends of the earth and trod the abysses of the depths.
I traveled over the waves of the sea and throughout all the earth,
and I took possession of every nation.
And after all this I sought rest. In what inheritance, then, would I rest?
And the Lord said to me, ‘You will dwell among Jacob, and Israel will be your inheritance.’
In his sanctuary I will serve,
and I was established in Zion, in my beloved city [?]. And I rested in Jerusalem; my authority [?], and I in it.”
And I was established in the midst of Israel, in the allotted inheritance of God.
Like a tall cypress on Mount Lebanon, and like a [?] on Mount Hermon.
And like a newly planted rosebush in Jericho.
And like a beautiful olive tree in the plain, and like a plane tree beside flowing waters, I grew tall.
I gave off a fragrance like cinnamon, and like choice myrrh I gave off a sweet fragrance.
And like a terebinth I made my branches take root. My branches are branches of glory and grace.
Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled with the fruit of my produce.
My memory endures from generation to generation.
And those who drink from me will long for me again.
All this is the book of the covenants of God Most High.
Knowledge of truth upon us, like the Tigris.
Who fills the Euphrates with wisdom, and like the Jordan in the days of harvest.
And like the Gihon in the days of the grape harvest.
Those who came first could not reach it, and those who came last did not even understand its end.
For his wisdom increased from the sea, and his counsel from the many depths.
I am like an irrigation channel from a river, and like a stream flowing abundantly into a garden.
And behold, my irrigation channel became like a river, and my river became like a sea.
I will spread my teaching like prophecy and distribute it to generations forever.
Look and see that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek it.
Wisdom for Instruction
There are three whom my soul hates, and I am utterly disgusted by their lives.
A proud poor man, a lying rich man, and an old man who is sexually immoral and lacking in sense.
How beautiful is the wisdom of the elderly!
And the mind and understanding of the honored.
Wisdom is the crown of the aged, and fear is their boast.
With my heart I called nine counsels blessed.
A man who rejoices in his children and who, while still alive, will see the downfall of his enemies.
And one who lives with a wise wife, and one who has not yoked an ox and a donkey together, and one who has not stumbled with his tongue and has not served anyone unworthy.
And blessed is the man who has found wisdom and has not been ruined by poverty and destitution.
He who has found wisdom is great, but it is not as great as
the fear of the Lord.
Hold fast to it, son, for nothing is like it.
Accept every pain, but not wounds of the heart. All evils are bad, but a woman's wickedness is worse.
There is no head more wicked than a snake's, and no enmity more wicked than a woman's.
May the lot of evils fall to her, and the inheritance of the ungodly.
Like a sandy uphill path beneath the feet of the elderly, so is a talkative wife to a gentle husband.
Do not be deceived by a woman's beauty, and do not let her wantonness make you weak.
Sin began with a woman, and because of her we continually die.
The husband of a wise wife is blessed, and the number of his days is doubled.
A wise wife is a good portion and the share of those who fear God.
My heart has dreaded these three things:
the anger of a city amid large assemblies,
false slander, worse than death,
the torment of the tongue, enough for everyone.
A wife who loves wine is a great source of anger, and she cannot conceal her disgrace.
A woman's promiscuity can be recognized in her eyes and eyebrows.
Keep a firm watch over a shameless daughter.
For just as a thirsty person opens his mouth and seeks to drink from any water, so a promiscuous woman offers her love to every man.
A humble wife is a gift from the Lord,
and she is beyond price. An angry and talkative wife is considered like a trumpet calling people to war.
My heart was grieved over these two things, and over the third anger came upon me:
a brave man weakened by poverty, and wise men despised by fools,
and a righteous man who turns to sins after much toil.
For a merchant does not save himself from sins.
For many have sinned through negligence.
And if they do not hold firmly to the fear of the Lord, their houses will quickly collapse.
A furnace fires earthen vessels, and a person's testing is in his thoughts.
For just as a tree’s fruit reveals its yield, so words reveal the thoughts in a person’s heart.
If you pursue righteousness, you will soon attain it and put it on like a robe of glory.
Every bird goes to its own kind, and truth goes to those who practice righteousness.
The speech of the righteous is always wisdom.
Wait for the right moment among fools, but take the initiative among counselors.
The speech of fools is tiresome, and their laughter stirs up sins.
But whoever reveals secrets destroys his own trustworthiness.
Love your friend and remain faithful to him.
But if you divulge his secret, do not pursue him any longer.
For just as a person destroys his enemies, so you have destroyed his friendship.
And you will no longer be able to regain him.
Do not pursue him, for he has gone far away from you.
For his secret has been revealed, and the hope of love has been cut off from the mind.
He makes his speech sweet before you and amazes you with his words, but afterward he twists his mouth and finds fault with your words.
The blows of a deceitful person are worse than a wound.
One who digs a pit for a friend will fill it himself.
Whoever seeks justice from the Lord will find vengeance.
Forgive your neighbor’s wrongdoing, and then your sins will be forgiven.
For if you hold a grudge against your neighbor, how will you ask the Lord for forgiveness?
Remember your end and cease your hostility.
Keep death and decay in mind, and keep the commandments.
Keep the covenant of the Most High in mind, and put aside your foolishness.
Remove strife and quarrelling from yourself, and your sins will diminish.
An angry man kindles strife, and a sinful man sets friends at odds, for he introduces slander into the midst of peace.
If you blow on a spark, it flares up, and if you spit on it, you extinguish it; both come out of your mouth.
Curse both the slanderer and the double-tongued person alike, for they have destroyed many who were at peace.
A three-faced tongue has driven peoples out from among the nations.
And it has destroyed mighty cities and demolished great palaces.
Whoever loves such a tongue finds no peace and cannot live in peace.
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not as many as have fallen by the tongue.
The death it brings is a cruel death, and hell is better than it.
May it not overcome the righteous, and may they not burn in its fire.
Those who have forsaken the Lord will fall into its hands; it will fall upon them like a leopard, destroying them.
My child, be careful, save yourself, and put a door over your mouth.
Tie up your silver and gold, and establish a measure and a weight for your words. Set a door at your mouth.
And be careful not to stumble through your tongue.
Whoever shows mercy lends to his neighbor, and whoever gives freely with his hand keeps the commandments.
Many have considered a loan a windfall and have caused their lenders great trouble.
When borrowing, they kiss hands, and for another person's possessions the borrower makes his voice pitiful.
And when the time comes to repay, he delays and offers tiresome words.
And if he is pressed very hard, he may repay half, and the other thinks to himself, “I have found a windfall.”
He heaps curses and slander upon him.
And he gains him as an enemy without cause.
And instead of honor, insults.
For the sake of the commandment, help the poor, and do not send him away without mercy.
Lose your silver for the sake of a brother and a friend, and do not let it rust away under a stone and be lost.
Give your treasures to the poor according to the commandment.
And it will be a shield for you against the enemy.
Let a generous man act as guarantor for a friend.
And do not forget the favor he did you by acting as your guarantor, for he gave himself in your place.
Acting as guarantor has ruined many and deprived them of prosperity.
And it has driven them to wander among a foreign nation.
Do not become a guarantor for a sinner, and a malicious man will come under his judgment.
The basic necessities of human life are water, fire, bread, clothing, and a house that covers one's shame.
Better is the life of a poor man under his own wooden roof than grand halls with another person's table.
Do not judge the great and the small by sight.
It is a miserable life to move from house to house, and wherever you stay as a stranger, you will find no freedom to speak.
Even if you strive and labor, it is useless, and on top of all this you hear harsh words.
Such as: “Come, get out of that house! Vacate the house you are in, for a dear brother and friend has arrived.”
This is hard for a man in his right mind to hear, for he has been reproached while still alive, and his life of hardship has been pointed out to many.
Words of instruction concerning friends and sons.
Whoever loves his son will frequently strike him with the rod.
Whoever disciplines his son will benefit from him and will be honored among his friends.
Whoever teaches his son makes his enemies break with envy and will rejoice before his friends.
His father died, yet he is not dead, for he left someone like himself in the world.
He saw his own life and was glad, and at his end he was not sorrowful.
He left behind an avenger against his enemies and secured favors for his friends.
Care for your son and bind up his wound.
A poorly trained horse turns out unruly, and an unrestrained son turns out according to his training.
Do not accustom him to insolence, lest you become sorrowful.
And do not flatter him, lest he give you bitter dregs and in the end fill you with blows.
Do not give your son free rein in his childhood, and do not dismiss the harm caused by his ignorance.
While he is still a child, bow down his neck.
So that you do not fall into disgrace because of him.
Better is a poor man who is obedient in serving as he is able than a rich man afflicted in his body.
Health and healing are better than gold and great wealth. A word of instruction concerning food.
There is no wealth better than bodily health, and nothing is better than joy of heart.
Death is better than a life of bitterness.
And just as delicacies are prepared and placed on a grave,
so are burnt offerings and sacrifices placed before idols. For whoever does this sees with his own eyes that they do not eat.
And he weeps and sighs.
Like a eunuch who embraces a virgin and is not satisfied.
Do not give yourself over to sorrow, and do not torment yourself with anxious thoughts.
A person's life is the joy of the heart.
Put sorrow away from you.
For there is no benefit in sorrow.
Anger and envy shorten one's days, and anxiety brings on old age before its time.
Concerning the delusions of anxiety.
Great sorrow wears away the bones.
And sorrowful anxiety drives sleep away. Severe illness keeps one awake.
The rich man labored to gather possessions, and in his rest he was filled with luxury.
The poor man labored, wearing down his life, and in his rest he found himself in need.
Whoever loves gold will not be justified, and whoever pursues lawlessness will be ruined.
Many were delivered to destruction because of gold, and their destruction came before them.
Blessed is the rich man who is found blameless and does not go astray in pursuit of gold.
A person's eye is evil.
So do not stretch out your hand toward whatever he looks at.

Think of what is good for yourself, and desire the same for your neighbor. For if you desire good for yourself and evil for others, the Lord will give you an evil time, seven times over, because you did not desire good for your neighbor. Do not set your mind on a foolish man or on [?] bread, and heed the instruction of wisdom. Always desire to see someone who is wise and makes peace. A person accustomed to turmoil resembles Satan, for Satan is not good, nor is such a person a peacemaker. Remove him from your midst and find peace away from him, so that others who did not know him will come to know him and will not blame you. They will drive him from city to city until he dies somewhere he does not know. My child, I encountered a foolish man and suffered much distress from him, for he was a dear and faithful servant, yet his mouth spoke bitterly. He recounted my words and those of my companion, my faithful spouse, before enemies, for mockery and jest. I instructed him with wise words, and he did not listen; I gave him a beating, and he obeyed. A club to the head is better for a foolish man than feather-filled pillows, for he is not corrected by wisdom. Do not delay in giving him what benefits him, for sooner or later he will be corrected by this.

Listen to me, my child, and do not despise me, and in the end you will find my words true.
Concerning vigorous deeds and other instructions.
Be energetic in your work, and illness will not come upon you.

Be generous with bread, and faithful people will praise you. Every person is a person, but choose the useful one who will help you in a time of distress, and give him your bread abundantly. Be a table for those in need, and their blessing upon you will reach everywhere.
Do not become angry over wine, for many have perished because of wine.
Wine without measure is bitterness of heart; a little wine is gladness and joy of heart.
Do not rebuke your companion at a drinking party.
And do not speak insulting words to him, lest evils enter among you through wine and you destroy one another.
My child, if you are the head of many, do not be proud over them; be like one of them.
And always care for them, and they will lay down their lives for you. Do not withhold from them the rewards you have promised.
Look after them at the tables, and regard their joy as your own.
Speak as an elder, for wisdom spoken with assurance is fitting for you.
I became like a gleaner following the grape gatherers.
And I was filled with the Lord’s blessing like a grape treader’s winepress.
Look and see that I have labored not only for myself, but for everyone who seeks wisdom.
Listen to me, rulers of peoples, and pay attention, leaders.
Do not give authority to a wife, children, a brother, or a friend during your lifetime.
While you are still alive, do not give yourself over to any mortal.
It is better for you that your children come to you than that you look to their hands for support.
Do not go to excess in any undertaking, and do not bring reproach upon your honor.
A stick, a load, and fodder for a donkey; bread, blows, and work for a slave.
Show your anger at him with blows, and you will find rest.
A yoke and a strap bow the necks of the proud.
And torture and shackles subdue a slave who does evil. Set him to work so that he does not become physically idle.
And do nothing unjustly.
But receive him as you would yourself.
Divination, enchantments, and dreams
stir up the minds of fools.
For many have been deceived by dreams and have fallen away from hope in the Lord.
The law will be fulfilled without falsehood, and the wisdom of the faithful will be complete.
A discerning man came to know many things, and wisdom was sent forth from him.
Concerning Useless Sacrifices. A burnt offering from injustice is a despised sacrifice.
For the Most High does not accept the sacrifices of the ungodly, nor does he forgive their sins because of their many burnt offerings.
Someone who offers burnt offerings from the possessions of the poor is like someone who slaughters a son before his father.
The bread they need is the life of the poor, and those who deprive them of it have the poor’s blood on their heads.
He who deprives his neighbor of [?] is a murderer of his neighbor.
He who cuts a hired worker’s wages shall be counted among those who shed blood.
What benefit do they produce except toil?
For one blesses and the other curses; whose voice will God hear?
So it is with a person who fasts because of his sins and then returns to those same sins.
Whoever keeps the law abounds in the commandments.
And whoever gives alms offers a blessing to the Lord.
Turning away from evil is pleasing to the Lord.
And salvation for souls is to escape Gehenna.
The sacrifice of a righteous man is acceptable, and let the memory of his sacrifices not be forgotten.
Serve the Lord generously, and do not be stingy with the fruit of your hands.
In all your giving, keep your face cheerful, and offer your tithes joyfully.
Do not look to the sacrifices of the lawless, for the Lord himself is the judge, and there is no favoritism before him.
He quickly hears the prayers of the one who has been wronged.
And he does not despise the widow or the orphan when he pours out his prayers before him.
And he will bring the merciless low and wipe out the multitude of the arrogant.
How beautiful is mercy in times of distress, like rain in times of drought!
Concerning prayers of petition
Have mercy on us, Lord, God of all, and look upon us.
Put the fear of you upon all the nations.
Raise your hand against foreign nations.
So that they may know you, as we also have known that there is no other God besides you, Lord.
Renew the wonders.
And glorify your right hand.
Arouse your indignation and pour out your anger.
Remove the adversary and wipe out the enemy.
Hasten the time and remember the judgment.
Let the enemy perish in the fury of fire, and let those who torment your people meet with ruin and destruction.
Crush the heads of wicked rulers who say, “There is no one else besides us.”
Gather the scattered tribes of Jacob, for they are yours, Lord, and they will bless you.
Protect yourself from deceitful advisers.
And do not consult with those who look at you suspiciously; also hide your words from those who envy you. Do not consult an ungodly man about piety or an unjust man about justice.
Do not consult a coward about war or a merchant about exchanging goods.
Do not consult a malicious man about gratitude, a merciless man about compassion, or a lazy man about any work.
Do not consult a hired worker about his own wages or a lazy servant about an order to do a great task. Do not share your plans with such people.
Instead, seek counsel from a godly man, especially if you know for certain that he has kept God’s commandments.
If you do not find such a man, rely on the counsel of your own heart, for you have no one more trustworthy than it.
And above all this, plead with the Most High to direct your paths in truth.
Words are the beginning of every task, and counsel comes before every action.
The paths of proverbs lead to the heart, for four outcomes arise from it: good and evil, life and death.
There is a shrewd man who instructs many but is of no use to himself.
There is one who is eloquent in words
and is found lacking in all wisdom, because grace has not been given to him by the Lord.
And wisdom is within him, and the fruit of his wisdom is trustworthy in his mouth.
A wise man will be filled with blessing, and many who see him will call him blessed.
And his name will endure forever.
Child, do not be greedy in all your pleasures, and do not overindulge in a variety of delicacies.
For many delicacies bring illnesses.
Many have died from gluttony, but whoever takes care of himself prolongs his life.
Honor the physician for your own needs, for he too was created by God.
But healing comes from the Most High.
There is a time when your healing is in their hands.
For they too will pray to the Lord that their work may succeed.
Shed tears over the dead, and do not disregard his written instructions.
Remain in mourning for a day or two, and then be comforted in your sorrow.
For sorrow often brings death, and sorrow of heart drains one's strength.
Put sorrow away from you.
And do not forget that you too will return there.
For he goes today, and you will go tomorrow.
When the dead man is at rest, let the remembrance of him cease.

Concerning people's crafts and instruction. How can a plowman become wise, or boast in his wooden goad? His work is to drive oxen and remain there with them. His conversation is among the young bulls.
His toil is among the cattle, and his heart is occupied with the furrows.
So it is with every carpenter and master builder who engraves carved images and fashions figures: he devotes his mind to the likeness of the image, and his toil completes the work.
So it is with the blacksmith at the anvil, who examines the red-hot rods of unworked iron.
The blast of the fire wastes his body, and the sound of the hammer deafens his ears.
He devotes his heart to completing his works.
Likewise, the potter sits at his work and turns the wheel held between his feet. He is continually concerned about his work, and everything he makes is valued.
His heart is wholly set on soundness, and his toil cleans his kiln.
All these people rely on their hands and have become skilled in their work.
Without them, cities cannot be built and populated.
But they must not sit in judges' seats.
And they must not declare judgments or instruction.
Rather, their prayers concern the work of their craft.
Concerning wisdom and various kinds of instruction. Wisdom will examine every profound matter and frequently utter prophecy.
He shall preserve the sayings of renowned men.
And he will occupy himself with the parables of their laws.
He will devote his heart to coming early to the Lord and appearing before the Most High.
He will open his mouth, and his sins will be forgiven.
He will examine words beyond understanding.
And he will make his teaching known and will always boast in the laws of the Lord's covenants.
Many will see his wisdom and bless him forever and ever.
And his name shall live on, and let his memory not be erased.
Listen to me, holy children, and blossom like roses planted beside flowing waters.
Bless the Lord for all his works.
With songs on your lips and the sounds of harps.
Give majesty to his name.
For he has looked from eternity to eternity, and nothing is astonishing in his eyes.
His praise spread out like rivers.
Likewise, his wrath will take possession of the nations.
The basic necessities for all people are water and bread, fire and iron, milk and honey, wine and oil, shelter and clothing.
All these things serve for good to those who do good, and for evil to the unholy.
They will curb the Creator's indignation.
Fire and hail, famine and death.
And these are for vengeance and for the destruction of the ungodly.
Look, I considered all these things in my mind and put everything in writing.

He has given people games of joking and laughter, apart from his laws and the sayings of his mouth. For he has also laid a heavy yoke upon these descendants of Adam, so that, when a person comes out of his mother's womb, he will quickly return to the mother of all, because of worthless envy and various chastisements.
The thought of evil until the day of the end.
From the glorious person who sits on a throne of glory to the one who sits on ashes instead of a cushion.
Envy and agitation and turmoil and hatred.
It destroys understanding during sleep at night.
Life is sustained by the work of good hands.
And the building of cities establishes your name. Yet a blameless wife is considered better than both of these.
Wine and the songs of musicians gladden the heart, but the love of wisdom does so more than both of these.
The eye longs for grace and beauty.
But a cheerful wife surpasses both of these.
Silver and gold.
They exalt greatly, but the fear of the Lord is above both of these.
Concerning death and various instructions. O death, how bitter is the memory of you to a man living at peace with his possessions!
O death, how welcome are your decrees to a man in need and failing in strength!
These decrees come from the Lord for all flesh.
And now, why do you hesitate at the will of the Most High?
The offspring of sinners are repulsive and loathsome.
The inheritance of sinners’ children will perish.
Even the children reproach their ungodly father.
Woe to you, ungodly people, who abandon the law of God Most High!
Keep the instruction of peace, my child,
and a good name forever.
May you be found tested and approved before all living beings.
A daughter is a secret source of sleeplessness to her father.
Keep a firm watch over a very shameless daughter,
and do not spend much time among women,
for a moth comes out of clothing, and evils come from women.
The wickedness of a man is better than the goodness of a woman. The beauty of a woman’s face is known by her brows, and a woman who causes shame brings disgrace.

Concerning the Lord’s creative command and various instructions. I remembered the works of the Lord, and I will recount what I saw. His works are at the command of the Lord’s word, and his will came to pass and was fulfilled.
The Lord knew every thought and looked upon the sign of eternity. He reveals hidden secrets,
and neither a word nor a thought was hidden from him,
and all his works are desirable.
He established good things, and who can have enough of recounting his glory?
In the firmament of the heavens,
the stars are an adornment, and the Lord illuminates the world from on high.
Look at the rainbow in the clouds and bless its Creator, for how beautiful is the light of its splendor!
The hand of the Most High established the tents of heaven.
At his gaze the mountains will melt, and at his will the south wind blows.
The sound of his thunder rebukes the mountains, and his northern storm gathers the winds.
He casts down a shower like birds in flight and lays it on the earth like assembled armies of locusts.
The beauty of its whiteness dazzles the eyes, and the heart marvels at its descent.
He scatters frost over the earth like salt, and when he freezes it, he makes it like spearheads.
Those who go down into the depths of the sea in ships tell of his awesome power, and we marvel at what our ears hear.
The Lord is fearsome, great, and exceedingly awe-inspiring.
When glorifying the Lord, raise your voice as much as you are able.
For beyond these there are still many hidden mysteries and wonders, for we have seen only a little of his works, and he has given wisdom to his servants. The words of Sirach are finished.
